name: Census
overview: The biblical practice of taking a census among the children of Israel, as recorded in Exodus, was more than a mere counting of people; it involved a sacred responsibility and a designated offering to the LORD. Each man twenty years and older was to pay a half shekel as a ransom for his soul, ensuring atonement and preventing plague among them (Exodus 30:12-16). This poll tax was equal for rich and poor alike, symbolizing the communal accountability before God. The census served not only to number the people but also to provide for the service of the tabernacle, as reflected in the numbering of over six hundred thousand men (Exodus 38:26). The topic also includes later censuses by Moses, David, and even the Roman Empire under Caesar, highlighting its ongoing significance in governance and divine order.
